name: Mind
description: Gives every step of a request the same running account of it (what the person asked, what it was resolved to mean, what was refused or corrected, what earlier steps found), carried from step to step instead of rebuilt, so a fast-tier model acts with a continuity one prompt per step cannot give it.
purpose: Keeps every step of a person's request acting on everything the request has established so far, at the cost of the fast tier.
approach: Carries one working stream per request from its first step to its answer, adds only what the admission gate lets in, and reuses the cached part instead of re-sending it.
out_of_scope: What carries across requests and sessions, and deciding which items are worth adding: the stream holds what it is given.
milestones: 1. A labelled set of multi-step requests exists in which a later step needs something established earlier (a refusal, a correction, the resolved request, an earlier finding), and rebuilt_per_step has a recorded result on it. 2. A carried stream scores at or above rebuilt_per_step on that set with the chat judge pass rate held and input cost per request no higher than rebuilt_full_context.
knowledge: The specification owner's design: a stream of consciousness focused only on the goal condition of this request, seeing only what relates to it, on the fast tier, because a coding agent is reliable through one long cached session. Read in the code on 2026-10-28, not yet reproduced on a live turn: each planner step is one fresh call (core/orchestrator_planning.py); a cached prefix of head and context layers spans the calls of a turn (core/prompt_layers.py); from the second step the transcript and the context block are swapped for a note saying they were given at step one (core/orchestrator_events.py, on by default in core/orchestrator_constants.py), and that block is where the resolved request, declined proposals, guidance, recent context and cards are prepended (core/orchestrator_run_begin.py); older observations collapse to one line past a recency window (core/planner_context.py). Swapping the context layer also changes the cached prefix, so later steps give up a cheap cache read of the context rather than a full-price one. The final answer still gets the full context. Deep work already runs as one continued session through the deep runner, so this solution concerns the in-process planning loop. From a founder's team meeting on 2026-10-27: the chat is weaker than a task sent to a coding agent because the library is a partial harness; the owner named three directions (near-perfect routing so hard requests reach a deep run, stored context so simple ones need none, or adopting an open-source harness, which the owner placed in the world, as an option to replace the coding agent for doing things: claim-reach), and wants high quality from a low-tier model through the structure of prompts and code, with the high tier kept for what matters most, such as plan generation.
measures_of_success: On multi-step requests no later step contradicts, re-proposes or ignores what an earlier step or the person established; the chat judge pass rate holds; input cost per request stays within that of re-sending the context from cache. Standing conditions: Never tell a model it saw something it was not given. Keep the stream inside the request's scope.
parameters: The implementation, the model tier, the stream's token budget and compaction point, and whether the context layer is re-sent, referenced or carried.
inputs: The person's message, the transcript, the resolved request and goal condition, the admitted context and each step's admitted observations.
outputs: Each step's view of the request (a carried message list or a rebuilt prompt), with the step's decision added to it.
effects: Planner-tier model calls; a provider prompt cache is written and read. No store writes.
usage_notes: Selected today: rebuilt_per_step. Compare rebuilt_full_context first, since it is one existing configuration flag, then a carried stream. Decision teamdec_a658ad84e023 (hold, no build).

name: Higher mind
description: Keeps, for each AI representative, one maintained high-level view across the set of quests assigned to it (what was decided, declined, learned and corrected there, and where the work is heading), anchored at the intent those quests serve and reading that intent's ancestors, so a request handled by the representative starts from the broad context of all its quests; a single quest's view is the narrow case. The view reaches only the representative's assigned quests and their ancestor intents, never other representatives' or people's.
purpose: Gives each AI representative a broad, high-level context across the quests it is assigned, so every request it handles starts from what that whole set and its intents have already settled.
approach: Maintains one standing view per representative across its assigned quests, anchored at the intent those quests serve, and hands each request the parts that bear on it, fenced to that representative's quests and their ancestors.
out_of_scope: Continuity within one request; the person's own reflections, intents and specification text, which are read and never rewritten; and creating or linking intents, which only a person does (the AI may ask).
milestones: 1. A labelled set of multi-session cases exists for representatives with several assigned quests under a nested intent hierarchy (a decline on one assigned quest then a related request on another, a correction applied later, chat then background work, a quest assigned to another representative, another person's intent), and separate_stores has a recorded result on it. 2. per_rep_assigned_view passes more of those cases than separate_stores, with no item reaching another representative's quests, a sibling intent or another person, and no time added before the reply.
knowledge: The specification owner's correction (2026-10-28): the higher mind is not per quest; each AI representative has its own higher mind, and every higher mind is associated with an intent, which is itself an ESOI specification. Intents nest recursively: a sub-intent arises as an implementation of a solution in its parent (life intents, then an organisation, then a product, then quests), a quest can sit under an intent at any level, and the depth differs by person and product; the host has backend support for this but no presentation of the hierarchy yet, and the owner asked to leverage it. What the host already has (read in its code 2026-10-28): intents owned by a person, a team or an organisation; one parent link per intent, active only while both sides state it; quest placements under an intent; an intent frame built by code for quest-scoped prompts that names the quest's intent and the level below it, not its ancestors; and a rule that a linked neighbour intent is shown only as far as its owner revealed. What the library has: the intent frame and lazily built quest specification (ground-in-intent), selection of the specification records a request concerns (spec-selection), conversation recall, feedback guidance, the scoped recent-context store, and per-representative learned notes and context preferences (select-context:rep), which carry no quest or intent scope; the scope tag fence compares flat tag sets and has no notion of ancestors. Missing: no view is kept per intent or per representative and intent; nothing walks the hierarchy upward for a request; the fence cannot express visible-to-descendants. The owner's further clarification (2026-10-28): the point of the higher mind is AI representatives with specifically assigned quests, so a representative holds a broader context at a high level across them; the representative and its assigned quests are the primary unit, associated with an intent in the hierarchy, and a single quest's view is the narrow case. How the host assigns them today (read in its code 2026-10-28): a quest lists its assigned representatives, each with the role the person gave it there; every autopilot persona on a quest is also assigned; a reverse lookup and an endpoint list a representative's quests; a goal can name the representative handling it; a representative registry holds its persona, home team and learned notes, which are kept for the representative as a whole. What is missing: no view spans a representative's assigned quests; its learned notes and context preferences are not tied to those quests or their intents; nothing derives the intent the assigned quests serve; and the fence cannot say a representative's own quests and their ancestors. Open recommendation: per_rep_assigned_view, since it is the owner's model and gives the representative's existing notes the fence they lack. The outcome history this solution keeps is what the subconscious's intuition draws on (remember-and-recall:outcome_precedents). A quest can have several representatives (owner's direction, 2026-10-28): each keeps its own view across its own assigned quests, a request reads only the view of the representative chosen to handle it (select-a-rep), and facts every representative on the quest needs, such as a decline or the quest's own state, are kept at the quest level so all of them see them.
measures_of_success: A decline holds across later requests under the same intent and its descendants; a correction is applied where it bears; chat and background work agree; a request in a child quest starts from its ancestors' views; no item reaches a sibling intent or another person; nothing adds time before the reply. When several representatives share a quest, a decline made with one holds for all of them. Standing conditions: Fence by the intent hierarchy on every read and write. Keep the person's own words verbatim. Never create or link an intent without the person.
parameters: The implementation, how many ancestor levels a request reads, the size of each view, when views are refreshed, and the model tier for any summary.
inputs: The representative, its assigned quests and their roles from the host, the host's intent hierarchy and quest placements, each finished request's outcome, and the stores' records.
outputs: For a request the representative handles: its standing view across its assigned quests and the views of their ancestor intents, with the source of each item, fenced to those quests and ancestors.
effects: Writes the maintained view in the background after a request; no work before the reply.
usage_notes: Selected today: separate_stores. The proposal is per_rep_assigned_view; per_quest_note is the narrow case and per_intent_cascade the view without representatives.

name: Request intake
description: Receives every request a person or program sends, by chat channel, terminal, the embedded package or mid-run input, and hands it on as one routed turn.
purpose: Let a person or a program reach the runner from wherever they work and be understood the same way.
approach: Accept each request through its own channel, describe what came with it, and route it to the handling it needs.
out_of_scope: Turning a request into an answer or a run (the Mind does that), classifying it as a message route (route-a-message does that) and reading its attachments (describe-an-attachment does that).
milestones: Every way in is a measured solution beneath this one (each with its own metric).
measures_of_success: Each way in passes its own metric; no request is misrouted or lost between channels.
inputs: A message, a terminal command, an attachment or a library call.
outputs: One routed turn with its context sources.
usage_notes: A container: its parts are measured, not the whole.

name: Subconscious
description: Draws on what the person's own material holds (their cards, files, notes, past conversations and recalled context) and decides at every step what of it enters the working stream, by whether it bears on the request's goal condition, with the scope fence applied once at that gate.
purpose: Keeps each request's working stream holding the part of the person's own knowledge its goal needs, so a fast model is neither misled by near misses nor buried in noise.
approach: Judges each candidate from the person's material against the request's goal condition and scope before it enters the working stream, settling clear cases cheaply and asking a small model only on the borderline.
out_of_scope: Finding the candidates (retrieval, card selection and reading keep their own specifications), and knowledge about the world beyond the person's own material.
milestones: 1. A labelled set of steps exists, each with candidate items marked needed, irrelevant, near miss or out of scope, and recency_window has a recorded result on it. 2. A goal-conditioned implementation admits more needed items than recency_window at the same or better precision, with no out-of-scope item admitted.
knowledge: The specification owner's design: the subconscious is the person's own knowledge and context; it does context assembly and tool calls and checks which context is worth showing to the mind. Assembly and reading are already specified (select-context, gather-evidence, search-cards-and-specs, recall-recent-context); this solution adds only the admission check, which no existing record owns. Today cards are filtered once at the start (core/card_filter.py) and observations are admitted by recency (core/planner_context.py). Its value grows with a carried stream, where an admitted item stays for every later step. On cheap-model routing a reviewer handed a decision argued with correct decisions while the same model asked one question of fact did well, so the borderline judge asks whether an item bears on the goal, never whether the plan is right. The specification owner's direction (2026-10-28): intuition is conceptually part of the subconscious. Recorded as outcome_precedents: at admission, past requests like this one and how they ended are surfaced to the working stream as a hint, never as a decision; the outcome history is kept by the long view (hold-the-intents). The anticipation engine predicts the next ask and recipes replay past successes; neither learns from how a turn ended, so this is new.
measures_of_success: Needed items are admitted, irrelevant and near-miss items are kept out, and no out-of-scope item is ever admitted, at no more than one small model call per step. Standing conditions: Apply the scope fence at the gate on every path. Treat an empty or near-miss lookup as not found.
parameters: Thresholds per source, the borderline band that calls the judge, the judge's tier, and the per-step token budget.
inputs: The goal condition, the turn's scope tags, and candidate items with their source and scores.
outputs: The admitted items with a one-line reason each, and the dropped ones with theirs, for the explanation of how an answer was reached.
effects: At most one small model call per step for borderline items; no writes.
usage_notes: Sits between retrieval and the working stream. Selected today: recency_window.
